skill.name: pr-description-writer
skill.description: Generates structured, reviewer-friendly pull request descriptions from branch context, diffs, commits, and PR metadata.
skill.summary: Creates organized PR descriptions with summaries, diagrams, file notes, and test plans.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: Static alerts in SKILL.md are Markdown formatting and documented Git or GitHub CLI examples for collecting PR context and optionally updating PR text. I found no prompt injection, obfuscation, secret exfiltration, or unauthorized command-execution intent. Users should still review generated PR content before publishing it.

remediation.issue: PR update examples can modify remote pull request metadata when copied and run.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should explicitly approve gh pr edit or gh pr create before publishing generated text.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use branch variables in several commands.
remediation.suggestion: Quote branch variables consistently in examples and prefer argument separators where supported.

- Exit code `0` + JSON output → PR exists, use the PR number for updates
2. **GitHub default** – `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` is authoritative
Once the description is generated, use `gh pr edit` to update:
Use horizontal rules (`---`) to separate major features.
- **API Change**: The `/api/endpoint` now returns X instead of Y.

content.value_statement: Reviewers lose time when pull requests lack context. This skill gathers branch changes and produces structured PR descriptions with summaries, diagrams, file notes, and test plans.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the current branch already has a GitHub pull request.
Identifies a base branch from PR metadata, GitHub defaults, remote HEAD, or common branch names.
Guides collection of commits, diffs, file stats, and uncommitted changes.
Drafts reviewer-focused Markdown with summaries, diagrams, grouped file notes, and test instructions.
Provides GitHub CLI examples for creating or updating pull request bodies.
limitations: Requires repository access and Git or GitHub CLI context for best results.
Does not verify test results unless the user runs the tests.
Generated descriptions need human review for sensitive changes and release language.
Command examples assume GitHub workflows and may need changes for other platforms.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature PR
use_cases.description: Turn a feature branch into a clear pull request description with scope, rationale, changed files, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Create consistent PR descriptions that help reviewers scan summaries, diagrams, risks, and test plans quickly.

use_cases.title: Document Infrastructure Changes
use_cases.description: Explain configuration, deployment, migration, and rollback details in a structured pull request body.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Current PR Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for the current branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pr-description-writer to create a PR description for my current branch. Include a summary, changed files, and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when a PR already exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pr-description-writer to review the existing PR for this branch and produce an updated description that preserves useful context.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Multi-Part Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for branches with several related changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pr-description-writer to summarize all commits and uncommitted changes from the base branch. Group the work by feature and include reviewer focus areas.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release-Sensitive PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for migrations, deployment steps, or risk notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pr-description-writer to create a PR description with migration notes, deployment steps, rollback guidance, breaking changes, and validation coverage.

output_examples.input: A branch adds a new API endpoint, updates service logic, and adds tests.
output_examples.output: A PR body with a short summary, key feature table, grouped files, API notes, automated tests, and manual checks.

output_examples.input: A branch changes a background job and introduces a new feature flag.
output_examples.output: A reviewer-focused description with a flow diagram, feature flag behavior, rollout notes, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A branch includes database migrations and deployment requirements.
output_examples.output: A PR description with migration details, deployment sequence, rollback plan, changed file groups, and risk notes.

best_practices: Review generated PR text for private details before publishing.
Include both automated and manual validation steps when relevant.
Place breaking changes and deployment steps in visible sections.
anti_patterns: Publishing a generated description without checking accuracy.
Describing only the latest commit when the branch contains multiple changes.
Omitting test steps or known risks for complex changes.

faq.question: Does this skill update pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and may offer to update a PR, but the user should approve any publishing action.

faq.question: Can it work without an existing pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. It can generate a description for a new PR by comparing the current branch to a base branch.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It is designed around Git and the GitHub CLI, with repository access for diffs, commits, and PR metadata.

faq.question: Does it run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It can include relevant test commands, but users must run and verify the tests themselves.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends ASCII or Mermaid diagrams for flows, pipelines, architectures, and decision paths.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but users should review output for secrets, internal details, and sensitive business context before publishing.
